additional_info.subject: ID0381306-DC/Si-D/FR[170001008] - Charging not possible DC1 CRM:00315001828
additional_info.body:
Hi Théo, good morning. I hope you are doing well.
Thank you for the cooperation. Thanks to your timestamp and logs I could recover the SECC logs to investigate the cause.
From the SECC's perspective, look at the voltage from CableCheck:
It's not reaching the 200V because of either:
Contactor QA13 or QA14 (one of them) is not closing properly. It looks like it's a “vibration” toggle, only when it's “closes” we get the small ammount of voltage and returns to 0 when it “opens”. I hope you understood what I mean with this.
Voltage transducer is not visualizing the voltage correctly, but from the logs' point of view, it seems like it's working:
So what this means is, the PLC is indeed sending the 200V but we are not checking that voltage before the contactors with TF5.
I am proactively checking if anyone is going to charge in this outlet. It will be difficult as the session will always stop in CableCheck. If it's possible to schedule a live session it would be great.
Otherwise, I need to send the regional partner to site and hope that the problem is indeed the contactors.
What is your opinion?
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0381306-DC/Si-D/FR[170001008] - Charging not possible DC1 CRM:00315001838
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
Mr. Theo raised a ticket for a DC1 not able to charge. If you are able to see the previous email, it seems like the contactor is not able to fully close and it's jumping from open to close and as such cannot main the voltage.
Please apply 24V to the QA13 and QA14, and measure continuity. If any of them are toggling between OL and continuity then you have the faulty one and needs replacement.
